transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. How can I help you today?

I'm here because I really need help fixing my face, especially this terrible acne and the horrible scars on my skin. It looks absolutely awful and makes me feel so anxious just being seen. Is there any way you can help me get rid of these flaws?
How much time do you spend each day thinking about or checking your appearance, and does it interfere with your daily activities?

I easily spend three or four hours every day obsessively checking myself in the mirror and trying to hide my skin with heavy makeup and layers of clothes. This whole routine takes so long that I'm constantly late for work, and it's completely disrupting my life. I just can't seem to stop doing it.
Have you ever considered that your concerns about your skin might be excessive or not as noticeable to others as they are to you?

My family and friends always tell me that my skin looks completely fine and that they can barely see any flaws. But I find that so hard to believe because when I look in the mirror, the acne and scars look incredibly obvious, ugly, and impossible to ignore.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidate was Body Dysmorphic Disorder, and based on this conversation, it remains the most consistent diagnosis. The patient exhibits preoccupation with perceived defects in appearance (skin and acne), spends excessive time (3-4 hours daily) on appearance-related behaviors (mirror checking, makeup application), experiences significant distress and functional impairment (being late to work), and demonstrates difficulty accepting reassurance from others that the flaws are not noticeable. These features strongly support Body Dysmorphic Disorder. No new information contradicts this diagnosis, and no other disorders from the allowed list better account for the symptom pattern.
